We now show that the coloring problem remains just as hard even if the algorithm knows the degeneracy of the graph before seeing the edge stream. I Theorem 21. Given as input an integer κ, followed by a stream of edges of an n-vertex graph G with degeneracy κ, a randomized one-pass algorithm that produces a proper (κ + λ)- 1 coloring of G requires Ω(n2 /λ2 ) bits of space.
